items.title: The 3 Core Rules of Pipes: Fullness, Bidirectional Sloshing & 'Full Pipes Are Happy Pipes'
items.subtitle: Pipes have zero built-in flow direction, obey gravity first, hold at least 5.0 m³ even when tiny, and have a true diameter of 1.30 m.
items.simpleRule: Fluid always flows from fuller/higher pipes to emptier/lower pipes in BOTH directions — so fill your pipes 100% full first, and gravity + sloshing problems vanish.
items.diagram:
WATER-LEVEL RULE (Pipes fill bottom -> top, left <-> right)

          [ C ]  <-- Won't fill until A & B are 100% full!
            |
      [ B ]-+
        |
  [ A ]-+
  (Gravity fills lowest pipes first; fluid sloshes BOTH ways <->)

  TRUE PIPE SIZE (v1.2.5.1):
  +-----------------------------------------------+
  |  Radius = 0.65 m  |  True Height = 1.30 m     |
  |  Volume = 1.327 m³/m (MINIMUM = 5.0 m³ floor) |
  |  Mk.1 = 300 m³/min   |   Mk.2 = 600 m³/min    |
  +-----------------------------------------------+
items.howTo: Unlike conveyor belts, pipes do NOT have a built-in one-way direction. Fluid moves in whichever direction has lower pressure — meaning it flows from fuller pipes to emptier pipes, and downhill before uphill. Every pipe segment has an internal tank (`FFluidBox`) whose volume is `1.3273 m³` per meter of length, **clamped to a minimum floor of `5.0 m³`** (even a `0.5m` stub holds `5.0 m³`!). A 4-way **Pipeline Junction Cross** holds `10.0 m³`, while a 3-way **T-Junction** holds `7.5 m³`. Until a liquid pipe is `100%` full (`Content == MaxContent`), it cannot pass upstream Head Lift through to the next segment.
items.stepByStep:
1. Watch the blue circular **Content Bubble** inside any Pipe Inspector: empty space at the top means fluid cannot push uphill past that segment yet.
2. Keep pipe runs short where possible — every segment `< 3.77 m`, Valve, and Pump still acts as a `5.0 m³` buffer that takes time to fill.
3. Pre-fill manifolds (or wait for machines to saturate) before turning on consumers so the entire line stays `100%` full and slosh-free.
items.proof: In `AFGBuildablePipeline::BeginPlay` (`0x18052a060`), pipe radius `mRadius` is `65 cm` (`0.65 m`), yielding horizontal `Height = 2.0 * 0.65 = 1.30 m` (general: `1.30 * cos(pitch) + (MaxZ - MinZ)`). Internal capacity `MaxContent` (`FFluidBox +0x18`) is `max(r^2 * pi * length_m, 5.0f)` where `FFluidBox::MINIMUM_VOLUME = 5.0` (`0x180f7b0b8`). In `AFGBuildablePipelineAttachment::BeginPlay` (`0x18052a610`), attachments enforce the same `5.0 m³` floor, and junctions with `connCount > 2` scale `MaxContent = connCount * 0.5 * 5.0` (`7.5 m³` for T-Junction, `10.0 m³` for Cross). In `AFGPipeNetwork::UpdatePressureGroups` (`0x1808f5ff0`), two pipes only merge into a shared Head-Lift Pressure Group if both have `fill >= 1.0` (`100%` full).

items.title: Head Lift Made Simple: The Water-Level Line, Free Gravity Siphons & True Limits (10/12m, 20/22m, 50/55m)
items.subtitle: Head Lift only measures vertical height above the source — horizontal distance is free, U-dips regain all height automatically, and physics allows a 10–20% cushion.
items.simpleRule: Head Lift is a flat horizontal altitude line across your world: go sideways as far as you want for free, dip into valleys for free, and only add a Pump when your pipe climbs above that ceiling.
items.howTo: Head Lift is purely **vertical altitude** (`Z` height in meters) measured from the centerline of a machine outlet or Pipeline Pump. Moving liquid `5 km` horizontally across flat ground uses **`0 m`** of Head Lift. If a pressurized pipe dips down `100 m` into a canyon and climbs right back up `100 m`, gravity pushes the water back up to its original altitude with **zero extra pumps**. Every fluid producer and pump also carries two separate Head Lift values in code: a **Design limit** (`10 m` / `20 m` / `50 m` shown in the UI and blue hologram snap ring) and a slightly higher **Physics Max** (`12 m` / `22 m` / `55 m`, scaled by `0.98` pressure loss). Still, build to the `10 / 20 / 50 m` design target so you stay out of flow throttling.
items.stepByStep:
1. Count vertical climb from the Pump's center (NOT from the ground) up to the highest point of the pipe.
2. When placing a second Pump uphill, move your hologram up the pipe until the spinning **blue snap ring** locks onto the exact `20 m` / `50 m` height ceiling.
3. Remember: stacking two Pumps right next to each other on a flat pipe does **NOT** add `50 + 50 = 100 m` — each Pump resets the ceiling starting from its own vertical altitude!
items.proof: In `AFGBuildablePipelinePump::BeginPlay` (`0x18052a990`) and `SetMaxHeadLift` (`0x18054f6f0`), `FFluidBox.AddedPressure` (`+0x40`) is initialized to `mMaxPressure` (`+0x848`: `22.0f` on Mk.1, `55.0f` on Mk.2, `12.0f` on `10m` extractors/machines), whereas `mDesignPressure` (`+0x84c`: `20.0f` / `50.0f`) drives UI gauges, warning audio (`CheckHeadliftDifferenceSounds`), and `AFGPipelinePumpHologram::FindHeadLiftSnappingLocations` (`0x180acc940`). In `AFGPipeNetwork::UpdatePressure` (`0x1808c1ca0`), group pressure transmits `(GroupPressurizedMax - MinZ - Height) * 0.98f` (`PRESSURE_LOSS = 0.98` @ `0x1819e305c`), yielding `21.56 m` (Mk.1) and `53.90 m` (Mk.2) effective lift when overfilled.

items.title: Flow Rate vs. Max Flow Rate: Why Half-Full Pipes Flow Half as Fast & Why Machines Pulse at 300/600
items.subtitle: Flow speed scales linearly with pipe fullness up to CapHeight (1.30m), while machines dump finished craft cycles in fast 300/600 m³/min bursts.
items.simpleRule: A pipe at 50% fullness can only move at 50% speed — and a 120 m³/min Water Extractor doesn't trickle at 120, it dumps fast 600 m³/min gulps that average out to 120!
items.diagram:
WHY PIPE FLOW DEPENDS ON FULLNESS (CapHeight = 1.30m)

  100% Full Pipe:  [====================] -> Max 300 / 600 m³/min
   50% Full Pipe:  [==========          ] -> Max 150 / 300 m³/min
   25% Full Pipe:  [=====               ] -> Max  75 / 150 m³/min

  WHY A 120 m³/min EXTRACTOR READS 300 or 600 m³/min:
  Extractor Internal Tank (200 m³) dumps every 1.0s craft cycle:
  +-----------+   Burst 600 m³/min (Mk.2)   +------------------+
  | Extractor |===========================>|  Avg = 120 m³/min|
  |  120/min  |   ...then pauses briefly    |  (Sawtooth Flow) |
  +-----------+                            +------------------+
items.howTo: **Flow Rate** is how fast fluid is moving right now; **Max Flow Rate** (`300` on Mk.1, `600` on Mk.2) is the speed limit of the pipe. Because liquid outflow scales linearly with `(Pressure - PortZ) / CapHeight`, a horizontal pipe that is only half full (`0.65 m` of its `1.30 m` height) physically caps its speed at `50%` (`150 m³/min` on Mk.1, `300 m³/min` on Mk.2). Meanwhile, every machine output port empties its internal `2 m³–50 m³` output buffer at the **connected pipe's full speed limit (`300` or `600 m³/min`)** until empty, then stops until the next craft cycle finishes — creating the normal oscillating sawtooth wave on pipe gauges.
items.stepByStep:
1. Never panic when a pipe gauge swings between `0` and `600 m³/min`: inspect it for `10–15` seconds to read the **average** flow, not a single instant.
2. If average flow is below your target and the Bubble Icon isn't `100%` full, your pipe doesn't have enough liquid inside it to hit its speed cap yet.
3. Pre-fill the line or feed from slightly above so gravity keeps the pipe full and unlocks `100%` flow speed.
items.proof: In `AFGPipeNetwork::UpdateFlow` (`0x1808f30e0`), liquid flow limit is multiplied by `clamp((Pressure - PortZ) / CapHeight, 0.0f, 1.0f)`, where `CapHeight = min(1.30f, Height)` on `AFGBuildablePipeline` (`0x18052a060`). In `UFGPipeConnectionComponent::Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput` (`0x1808cb4e0`), `maxPush` (`+0x298`) is `10,000 L/s` (`600 m³/min`), causing extractors (`Build_WaterPump` `mItemsPerCycle = 2000` L every `1.0s` = `120 m³/min`) and refineries to dump integer liter batches at `min(machineStack, pipeSpace, cap)` as fast as the attached pipe allows.

copySnippets.label: CapHeight Flow Formula
copySnippets.text: EffectiveFlow = FlowLimit * clamp((Pressure - PortZ) / CapHeight, 0, 1)

items.title: Liquid vs. Gas: Why Gases Climb 2,000m Towers With Zero Pumps (And Why Fluid Buffers DO Work on Gas!)
items.subtitle: Gas networks skip gravity and Z-elevation completely (Pressure = 200 * fill), and contrary to the 2022 manual, Fluid Buffers, Valves, and 1-way Pumps all work on Gas.
items.simpleRule: Gases completely ignore gravity and climb straight into orbit with ZERO Pumps — and YES, Fluid Buffers store gas and Valves control gas normally!
items.diagram:
LIQUID vs. GAS IN THE ENGINE (v1.2.5.1)

  LIQUIDS (Water, Oil, Fuel, Acid)   |  GASES (Nitrogen, Rocket/Ionized Fuel)
  -----------------------------------+---------------------------------------
  [Machine]                          |  [Machine / Blender]
     |                               |     |
     +--[Pump Needed Above 10m!]     |     +-- ZERO Pumps Needed (2,000m+ UP!)
     |                               |     |
     +--[Buffer] (breaks Head Lift   |     +--[Buffer] (WORKS! Stores 400/2400m³
     |            if < 100% full!)   |     |           & outputs at P=200*fill)
     v                               |     v
  Gravity + Pressure Groups          |  Pure Density Pressure = 200 * fill%
items.howTo: **Gases (`RF_GAS`)** — **Nitrogen Gas**, **Rocket Fuel**, **Ionized Fuel**, **Dark Matter Residue**, and **Excited Photonic Matter** — use a completely separate physics loop (`TickPhysics_Gas`) that **ignores height (`Z`) and gravity completely**. You can pipe Nitrogen or Rocket Fuel straight up a `2,000 m` vertical sky-tower at `600 m³/min` without placing a single Pump. **Red-Team Myth Busted:** The 2022 manual claimed Fluid Buffers do not work on Gas because Buffers depend on Head Lift. In `v1.2.5.1`, **Fluid Buffers work 100% normally on Gas** (`Pressure = 200 * fill`, `400 / 2,400 m³` storage), and **Valves & Pumps still act as 1-way check valves and Flow Limiters on Gas** — only Pump *Head Lift* is ignored.
items.stepByStep:
1. Delete ALL Pumps you only placed for vertical lift on Nitrogen Gas, Rocket Fuel, or Ionized Fuel lines — you save `4–8 MW` per pump!
2. Use Fluid Buffers freely on Gas buffers (e.g., Rocket Fuel surge storage or Drone Port feeds): gas equalizes smoothly by `%` fullness (`Pressure = 200 * Content / MaxContent`).
3. Only place a **Valve** on a Gas pipe if you specifically want to cap flow rate (`m³/min`) or prevent backflow (`1-way` diode).
items.proof: In `AFGPipeNetwork::UpdateSimulation` (`0x1808f64b0`), resource form `+0x2c8 == 3` (`RF_GAS`) dispatches to `TickPhysics_Gas` (`0x1808f1670`) + `UpdateFlow_Gas` (`0x1808f3770`). `TickPhysics_Gas` skips `UpdatePressureGroups` and `MinZ` completely, setting `Pressure = 200.0f * (Content / MaxContent)` (`0x1808f16ac`) and zeroing `MaxPressure` (`+0x3c = 0`) on every `FFluidBox` in the network — including `AFGBuildablePipeReservoir` (`400 / 2400 m³`). `UpdateFlow_Gas` reads `PipeJunction[+0x18/+0x1b/+0x1c]` (`bIsDirectional` and forward/reverse allow flags) and clamps by `min(BoxA[+0x30], BoxB[+0x30])`, proving Valves and Pumps still enforce 1-way gating and flow limits on Gas.

copySnippets.text: RF_GAS: Pressure = 200 * (Content/MaxContent) | Ignores Z & Head Lift | Buffers & Valves WORK

items.title: Pumps, Valves & Fluid Buffers: What Each Part Actually Does (And the Unpowered Pump vs. Closed Valve Trap)
items.subtitle: Unpowered Pumps pass flow but reset head lift to 0m; Closed Valves block flow but still transmit 98% head lift forever; <100% Fluid Buffers wipe upstream head lift.
items.simpleRule: Power off a Pump -> Head Lift drops to 0m (but fluid can still flow!). Close a Valve to 0 -> Flow stops completely, yet 98% Head Lift STILL passes through! Inline Fluid Buffer < 100% -> Wipes all upstream Head Lift!
items.diagram:
COMPONENT BEHAVIOR CHEAT-SHEET (LIQUID NETWORKS)

  Part               | Blocks Backflow? | Limits Flow? | Passes Upstream Head Lift?
  -------------------+------------------+--------------+-----------------------------
  Powered Pump       | YES (1-way)      | No (600 cap) | Resets & adds +20m / +50m
  Unpowered Pump     | YES (1-way)      | No (600 cap) | NO! Resets Head Lift to 0m
  Open Valve         | YES (1-way)      | Set Limit    | YES (98% passes through!)
  Closed Valve (0)   | YES (blocks ALL) | 0 m³/min     | YES (98% STILL passes! Q-47)
  Buffer (<100% full)| No (2-way)       | Bottom 1.5m* | NO! Strips to own 0..8m/12m
  Buffer (100%+over) | No (2-way)       | Full speed   | YES (joins Pressure Group)
  *Buffer CapHeight = 1.5m: scales max outflow 0->100% over bottom 75m³ / 300m³
items.howTo:
Every pipe attachment plays a specific hydraulic role — and two common traps catch even veteran builders:
1. **Powered vs. Unpowered Pump:** Both act as 1-way diodes (blocking backflow) with a `600 m³/min` cap, NOT `300`. When powered, a Pump sets its exit Head Lift to `20m (22m max)` or `50m (55m max)` measured from the Pump's center. When **unpowered or paused**, it sets `AddedFactor = 0`, wiping all Head Lift to `0m` (though gravity/downhill flow still passes through!).
2. **Valves (1-Way Flow Caps + Head-Lift Pass-Through):** A Valve sets exact float flow limits (`0..600 m³/min`, zero quantization despite the gauge needle!) and **passes `98%` of upstream Head Lift even when closed to `0 m³/min`** (`Q-47`).
3. **Fluid Buffers (`400 m³` / `2,400 m³`):** Any inline Buffer that is **less than `100%` full (`GroupIdx = -1`) strips all upstream Pump/Water-Tower Head Lift** and replaces it with the Buffer's own `0..8 m` / `0..12 m` liquid column! Its bottom `1.5 m` (`CapHeight`) also smoothly ramps max outflow from `0% -> 100%` across `0..75 m³` (Small) or `0..300 m³` (Industrial).
items.stepByStep:
1. Never leave an unpowered Pump on a flat or rising line — dismantle it or power it, or it becomes a `0 m` Head Lift wall.
2. Never place a Fluid Buffer *in the middle* of a pressurized climb unless the Buffer sits **above** your consumers or is kept `100%` overfilled.
3. Use a Valve whenever you need a `0 MW` one-way backflow preventer that preserves full upstream Head Lift.
items.proof: `AFGBuildablePipelinePump::Factory_Tick` (`0x180534860`) sets `AddedFactor` (`+0x814`) to `1.0f` if producing (`+0x70c != 0`) or `0.0f` if unpowered/paused, and `UpdateDefaultFlowLimit` (`0x180558ed0`) clamps `mDefaultFlowLimit` to `min(10.0f, connectedPipeBox->FlowLimit)`. On Valves (`mMaxPressure = 0`), `SetUserFlowLimit` (`0x180551cd0`) writes full `float` `mUserFlowLimit` (`+0x854`) into `FFluidBox.FlowLimit` (`+0x800`), while `UpdatePropagatedPressure` (`0x1808f6460`) still copies `98%` upstream pressurized height whenever `bIsDirectional` is set. On `AFGBuildablePipeReservoir::BeginPlay` (`0x180529ea0`), `Height = 8.0m / 12.0m`, `CapHeight = 1.5f` (`+0x7dc`), `MaxOverfillPct = 0.01f` (`+0x7e8`).

items.title: Perfect Pipe Manifolds: Top-Feeding, Pre-Filling the 50 m³ Machine Buffers & Loop Backs
items.subtitle: Feed machine inputs from level or above (never below), fill machine internal buffers before startup, and close long manifolds into a loop to kill sloshing.
items.simpleRule: Build your main header pipe LEVEL WITH or ABOVE machine inputs, let the 50 m³ machine buffers fill before powering consumers, and connect both ends into a loop on big rows.
items.diagram:
BAD (Bottom-Fed: starves machines!)     GOOD (Top-Fed Gravity Lock + Loop)

   [Refinery]   [Refinery]   [Refinery]     ===+==========+==========+===
       ^            ^            ^             |          |          |  |
       |            |            |             v          v          v  |
  ====<+>==========<+>==========<+>=        [Refinery] [Refinery] [Refinery]
  (Whole manifold must stay 100% full       (Gravity drops fluid straight into
   just to touch machine ports!)             each port & Loop kills end bounce!)
items.howTo: Because pipes are bidirectional and obey gravity first, a **bottom-fed manifold** forces your entire pipe network to sit at `100%` capacity up to port height at all times — the moment one machine takes a gulp, *every* machine drops below port height simultaneously. Flip the rule around: elevate your manifold spine **level with or `2–4 m` above** the machine inputs so gravity pushes fluid straight down into each machine port (`PortZ` favors downhill drops first!). Second, every factory machine has an internal `50 m³` fluid input tank: if you connect empty machines to a live manifold, they violently gulp fluid and trigger wave sloshing. Pre-fill the manifold and machine inputs first, and on high-flow (`450–600 m³/min`) lines, loop the far end of the manifold back to the start so fluid feeds from **both directions**.
items.stepByStep:
1. Route your main manifold Junction Crosses **above** (or level with) the machine fluid intake ports (`2m–4m` elevated spine is ideal).
2. Turn consumers to Standby (or wait `1–2` minutes before connecting power) so the manifold pipes AND each machine's `50 m³` internal input tank fill to `100%`.
3. For `6–16+` machines on one line, bridge a return pipe from the last Junction back to the first Junction (forming a closed loop) to eliminate end-of-line backflow bounce.
items.proof: In `AFGPipeNetwork::RebuildUpdateList` (`0x1808e4f40`), each `PipeJunction` computes `PortZ = 0.0f` when `conn.WorldZ < Box.MidZ` and `(Box.MaxZ - Box.MinZ)` when `conn.WorldZ >= Box.MidZ`. On a top-fed drop pipe (`MaxZ` at spine, `MinZ` at machine), the upper spine connection sits at `PortZ = MaxZ - MinZ` (`> 0`), while the machine port sits at `PortZ = 0.0f` (`MinZ`), guaranteeing that gravity drains the drop leg into the machine buffer first (`UpdateFlow` `0x1808f30e0` computes `max(Pressure - PortZ, 0)`).

copySnippets.text: 1. Feed ABOVE inputs | 2. Pre-fill 50m3 buffers | 3. Loop both ends

items.title: Why 600 m³/min Mk.2 Pipes Lose Flow at the First Junction — And the 3 Foolproof Fixes
items.subtitle: Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput discards unpushed tick rate whenever back-slosh fills the first pipe segment — and a 600 m³/min source has zero spare headroom to catch up.
items.simpleRule: Never let back-sloshing hit the pipe segment touching a 600 m³/min machine or Miner: drop straight down into the first Junction, loop your manifold, or lock it with a Pump diode.
items.diagram:
WHY 600 m³/min LINES LOSE FLOW (Non-Banked Tick Bug @ 0x1808cb4e0):
  [600 Source] ---> [Pipe #1] <=== (Back-slosh fills Pipe #1!)
                      ^--- Machine tries to push `cap` liters, hits full pipe,
                           and THROWS AWAY the unpushed time budget forever!

  3 FOOLPROOF 600 m³/min FIXES:
  Fix A (Gravity Drop):  [600 Source]--+--[Downhill Pipe]--> <First Junction>
  Fix B (Two-Way Split): [600 Source]---> <T-Junction> ==+==> Loop Left
                                                         +==> Loop Right
  Fix C (Pump Diode):    [600 Source]--->[Pipe]-->[Pump >>]--> <Manifold>
items.howTo: Players have noticed for years that a **single Mk.2 pipe running at `600 m³/min`** (e.g., `600` Pure Crude Oil or a `250%` Blender/Refinery) mysteriously settles around `570–590 m³/min` when feeding a long manifold. The exact `v1.2.5.1` binary proof is in `Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput` (`0x1808cb4e0`): every factory tick, a machine calculates how many liters (`cap`) it is allowed to push into its output pipe (`maxPush = 600 m³/min`). If downstream sloshing briefly fills that very first pipe segment so `pipeSpace < cap`, the machine pushes fewer liters **yet still subtracts the FULL `cap` from its time accumulator**! Because `maxPush` itself caps at `600 m³/min`, a `600 m³/min` producer can **never catch up** from even a single clipped tick. All 3 fixes work by preventing back-slosh from ever filling that first source segment:
items.stepByStep:
1. **Fix A (Best & Cheapest — Split at Source):** Place a **T-Junction (`7.5 m³`)** or **Junction Cross** directly as close to the `600 m³/min` producer as possible, feeding TWO Mk.2 branches (`300 + 300 m³/min`) into a **looped manifold** so neither downstream branch ever hits `600` or reflects a bounce wave.
2. **Fix B (Gravity Drop-In):** Raise the `600 m³/min` producer (or drop the manifold `2–4 m` lower) immediately after the first pipe so `PortZ = 0` keeps the exit pipe drained into the manifold.
3. **Fix C (Pump Diode Wall):** Place a **powered Pump** (or **Open Valve set to `600`**) right after the first segment so downstream manifold slosh cannot travel backward (`bIsDirectional = 1`) into the source segment, plus loop the downstream manifold.
items.proof: In `UFGPipeConnectionComponent::Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput` (`0x1808cb4e0`), `acc = dt + timeAcc[+0x290]`, `budget = acc * float(maxPush[+0x298])`, and `cap = floor(budget)` where `maxPush = 10,000 L/s = 600 m³/min`. It computes `pushed = min(stackCount, spaceLiters, cap)`, adds `pushed * 0.001` to `FFluidBox.Content`, and writes `timeAcc[+0x290] = (budget - cap) / maxPush` instead of `(budget - pushed) / maxPush`. Whenever `spaceLiters < cap` on any tick, `cap - spaceLiters` liters of rate credit are permanently deleted, bounding sustained throughput below `600 m³/min` unless backflow into the source box is prevented.

copySnippets.label: 600m3/min Fix
copySnippets.text: Prevent back-slosh at source: Split immediately into 2x300 loop, drop downhill, or add 1-way Pump/Valve diode.

items.title: Byproduct Recycling Without Deadlocks (Aluminum Water, Sulfuric Acid & Heavy Residue)
items.subtitle: Never merge byproduct fluid directly into a fresh extractor line at the same elevation — use dedicated byproduct machines, a VIP priority junction, or a separate consumer.
items.simpleRule: Fresh Water Extractors will happily flood your recycled Water pipe and jam your Refineries unless you separate them (Dedicated Machines) or force the byproduct onto the bottom VIP port!
items.diagram:
ALUMINUM DEADLOCK VS. THE 3 ROCK-SOLID FIXES

  DEADLOCK:  [180 Fresh] ---> <Cross> <--- [60 Byproduct]  (240 > 180? NO!
             Extractor fills pipe to 100%, Scrap Refinery backs up & halts!)

  FIX 1 (GOLD STANDARD — Zero Circuits, 100% Jam-Proof):
    [Fresh Extractors] ===> [Refineries A & B] (100% fresh water only)
    [Byproduct Water]  ===> [Refinery C]       (100% recycled water only!)

  FIX 2 (VIP / Gravity Priority — see P-10 for full circuit):
    [Fresh Water] -----> (Top PortZ)   <-- Blocked while bottom has water!
    [Byproduct Water] -> (Bottom PortZ) -> [Alumina Refineries]
items.howTo: Whenever a factory machine has a fluid byproduct (like **Aluminum Scrap** outputting `120 m³/min` Water, or **Uranium / Plutonium / Blender** loops outputting Sulfuric Acid or Nitric Acid), if its output pipe fills to `100%`, **the machine stops completely**. Simply merging a fresh Water Extractor with a byproduct pipe into a flat Junction Cross causes a deadlock the moment any belt backs up, because the extractor fills the shared manifold to `100%` and blocks the byproduct from exiting. Here are the 3 best fixes ranked from easiest to most flexible:
items.stepByStep:
1. **Dedicated Byproduct Machines (Recommended — Zero Valves/Pumps):** Split your Alumina/Acid consumer machines into two separate pipe networks: run `N` machines strictly on Fresh Extractors, and run `M` machines strictly on Byproduct output (e.g., `240 m³/min` Scrap water feeds `1.33` Alumina Refineries directly with zero fresh water attached!).
2. **VIP / Gravity Priority Merger (`P-10`):** If all machines share one loop, feed **Byproduct** into the **bottom port** of a vertical Junction Cross and **Fresh Water** into the **top port** (`P-10`). The Junction drains the bottom byproduct 100% first!
3. **Alternate Sink Consumer:** Route leftover Water directly into **Coal Generators** or **Wet Concrete** Refineries (or Packager -> AWESOME Sink as a last resort) — never connect fresh extractors to that drain line.
items.proof: `AFGPipeNetwork` has no built-in priority between horizontal ports at the same `Z`: `RebuildUpdateList` (`0x1808e4f40`) assigns equal `PortZ` to equal-height ports, so a `100%`-pressure fresh extractor balances upstream pressure to `100%` and leaves zero `headroom_receiver` for byproduct `Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput` (`0x1808cb4e0`). Separating networks or placing Fresh at `PortZ = MaxZ - MinZ` (`P-10`) guarantees byproduct `avail_donor` always drains first.

copySnippets.label: Best Byproduct Rule
copySnippets.text: Best: Separate networks (Fresh-only machines + Byproduct-only machines). Combined: Bottom Port = Byproduct, Top Port = Fresh.

A `2.8m` pipe (`ratio 1.4`) costs `1x`; splitting it into four `0.7m` stubs and dismantling the pipes first (or painting them different swatches to block `Merge`) refunds **`4x`**!
- **Foundation-Free Fluid Buffer Stacking (`Q-76`):** Aim a Fluid Buffer directly at another Buffer (`0x180af23b0`) to snap it flush on top (`+8m` / `+12m`), spin yaw freely, and retract its support legs (`ClearFeetOffsets`).

Complete 14-point adversarial audit comparing the 2022 Update 5/6 Plumbing Manual against `v1.2.5.1 (CL#520140)`:
1. **Pipe Diameter / Head Lift = `1.2 m`:** **CLARIFIED** -> `mRadius = 0.65 m` (`1.30 m` full diameter).
2. **Horizontal Pipe Fullness Scales Flow (`50%` full = `50%` speed):** **CONFIRMED** (`CapHeight` scaling in `UpdateFlow`).
3. **Machines Empty at Connected Pipe Max (`300/600`):** **CONFIRMED** (`maxPush = 10,000 L/s`).
4. **`12%` Machine/Pump Head-Lift Tolerance (`12m / 22m / 55m`):** **CLARIFIED** -> Not a magic `12%`; machines (`+20%`) and pumps (`+10%`) literally store separate `mDesignPressure` (`10/20/50`) and `mMaxPressure` (`12/22/55`) fields, scaled by `0.98`.
5. **Pumps Don't Stack / U-Dips Are Free / Gravity Stacks After Pump:** **CONFIRMED** (`UpdatePressureGroups`).
6. **Unpowered Pumps Block Head Lift (`0m`) While Passing Flow:** **CONFIRMED** (`AddedFactor = 0.0`).
7. **Pump Blue Snap Ring Stops at `100 m` & Traverses Junctions:** **CONFIRMED** (`10,000 cm` spline cap).
8. **Fluid Buffers Do NOT Work on Gas (Page 5):** **BUSTED** -> `TickPhysics_Gas` simulates Buffers identically (`400/2400 m³`, `Pressure = 200 * fill`).
9. **Buffers Need `75 m³` / `300 m³` (`1.5 m` Port Height) Before Full Output:** **BUSTED / CLARIFIED** -> Port Z is `0.0 m`; `1.5 m` is `CapHeight`, which linearly ramps output from `0% -> 100%` over `0..75 m³` / `0..300 m³`.
10. **Valve Flow Gauge Display Bug:** **CONFIRMED** -> `0..127` UI byte quantization; actual Valve `mUserFlowLimit` is an exact unquantized float.
11. **600 m³/min First-Junction Flow Loss:** **CLARIFIED** -> True root cause is `Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput` (`0x1808cb4e0`) discarding `(cap - space)` time budget on clipped ticks.
12. **Top-Fed Manifolds + Pre-Fill + Loops:** **CONFIRMED** (`PortZ = 0` at lower ports).
13. **Inline Flow Equalizers / Compensators (Page 15):** **BUSTED** -> Placing `< 100%` Buffers inline strips upstream Head Lift (`GroupIdx = -1`).
14. **VIP / VOP / Overflow / Water Tower / Two-Way Pump:** **CONFIRMED & UPGRADED** -> `0-MW` Valve VIP (`P-10`) & `0-MW` Closed-Valve Pipe Tower (`P-12`).

items.subtitle: Instant field-repair diagnostic table covering Floor Hole disconnects, 600 m³/min drift, inline Buffer head-lift loss, 100-hop manifolds, and instant single-segment flushing.
items.simpleRule: Check in order: (1) Broken connection (rebuild Floor Hole pipes!), (2) Head Lift stripped (unpowered Pump, <100% inline Buffer, or >100 boxes), (3) 600m³/min back-slosh!

30-SECOND PIPE DIAGNOSTIC FLOWCHART

  [Pipe Full -> Next Pipe Empty?] --> Rebuild pipe onto Floor Hole/Support (Check #1)
               |
               v
  [Climbing Pipe Stops Halfway?] ---> Check: Unpowered Pump? Inline Buffer <100%? >100 boxes?

items.howTo:
**Q1: Pipe A is 100% full, Pipe B right after a Floor Hole or Support is 0% empty!** -> **Cause:** Missing weld (e.g., Floor Hole placed *onto* an existing pipe fails `ConfigureActor` `0x180ac7b10`, or upgrading/rebuilding broke the snap). **Fix:** Delete & rebuild the two connected pipe segments onto the Floor Hole.
**Q2: My 600 m³/min Mk.2 pipe only averages 570–590 m³/min!** -> **Cause:** Back-slosh clips `Factory_Internal_PushPipeOutput` (`0x1808cb4e0`). **Fix:** Split immediately at the producer via a T-Junction into a looped manifold, or drop downhill (`P-07`).
**Q3: I added a Fluid Buffer inline and my uphill machines starved!** -> **Cause:** Any Buffer `< 100%` stays ungrouped (`GroupIdx = -1`), resetting upstream Head Lift to `0..8m/12m`. **Fix:** Put the Buffer on a side Tee or place a Pump *after* the Buffer.
**Q4: Huge flat/rising manifold loses Head Lift near the far end even with a Water Tower!** -> **Cause:** `FindTopMostPressureGroupIndex` (`0x1808cdf00`) aborts at `100` consecutive fluid boxes! **Fix:** Merge tiny pipe segments or add a Pump partway down.
**Q5: Wrong fluid got stuck inside a single pipe segment!** -> **Cause:** First-wins lock (`0x1808f2850`). **Fix:** `Ctrl`-tap Mk.1 <-> Mk.2 upgrade (`0x18055a820`) or snap/dismantle a Valve (`Split` `0x180554770`) to erase just that segment's fluid instantly (`Q-74`)!
**Q6: Can Pumps go on horizontal pipes?** -> Yes (`bIsDirectional = 1`), and they add `20/50 m` lift ready for the next climb, OR use a `0-MW` Valve if you just want 1-way anti-slosh.
**Q7: Do I need Pumps for Nitrogen / Rocket Fuel / Ionized Fuel?** -> **Never!** Gases ignore elevation (`P-04`).
**Q8: Do I need Pumps on a pipe that dips into a valley and goes back up?** -> **Never**, as long as the exit isn't higher than the original source Head Lift (`P-02`).
**Q9: Does a Valve flow limit round to coarse integers?** -> **No!** `SetUserFlowLimit` (`0x180551cd0`) stores exact floats; only the visual gauge needle quantizes.
**Q10: My Fluid Train Platform can't sustain 600 m³/min!** -> **Cause:** `27.0s` docking freeze (`P-09`). **Fix:** Hook BOTH ports (`1,200` burst) into an Industrial Fluid Buffer.
**Q11: My Aluminum Scrap Refineries keep stalling every 15 minutes!** -> **Cause:** Fresh Extractors flood the recycled pipe (`P-08`). **Fix:** Dedicate `100%` recycled-only Refineries OR use a `0-MW` VIP (`P-10`).
**Q12: Can I stack Fluid Buffers in mid-air without foundations?** -> **Yes!** Aim a Fluid Buffer directly at another Buffer to snap vertically & retract legs (`Q-76`).
items.stepByStep:
1. When debugging any broken fluid build, inspect **Connections -> Elevation/Pumps -> Inline Buffers -> Box Count (>100) -> 600 m³/min Source Back-Slosh** in that exact order.
2. Use `Ctrl` Mk.1 <-> Mk.2 hot-swap (`Q-74`) whenever you want to erase fluid in one faulty pipe segment without flushing the whole network.

items.title: Power Plant Plumbing: Fuel Generator Auto-Flush (0x180531cb0) & Nuclear 10 m³ Water Gulps (0x18052d290)
items.subtitle: Fuel Generators automatically call RemoveAllFromIndex when a different valid fuel arrives (no manual tank drain needed!), whereas Nuclear Plants require 10,000 L (10 m³) batches before CanLoadSupplemental triggers.
items.simpleRule: Upgrading a power plant to Turbofuel / Rocket Fuel? Only flush the pipes — Fuel Generators auto-flush themselves! And give every Nuclear Power Plant a full pre-filled water pipe so its 10 m³ gulp never starves!
items.diagram:
GENERATOR PIPE PULL RULES (v1.2.5.1)

  Fuel Generator (0x180531cb0):               Nuclear Power Plant (0x18052d290):
  [New Fuel] -> [Pipe] -> [Fuel Gen]          [Water Pipe] -> [Nuclear Plant 50 m³ Slot]
  1. Flushes old fuel via RemoveAllFromIndex   Requires >= 10,000 L (10 m³) per load!
  2. Pulls up to 50 m³ slot size every tick    (Coal only needs 1,000 L = 1 m³ per load!)
items.howTo: Unlike `AFGBuildableManufacturer` (Refineries/Blenders, which lock up if old fluid remains), `AFGBuildableGeneratorFuel::Factory_CollectFuel` (`0x180531cb0`) checks if the incoming pipe fluid differs from the current fuel slot and **automatically flushes the generator's internal tank (`RemoveAllFromIndex`)** before loading up to `50 m³` (`GetSlotSize`). Meanwhile, `CanLoadSupplemental` (`0x18052d290`) requires **`1,000 L` (`1 m³`)** of Water per batch on Coal Generators, but **`10,000 L` (`10 m³`)** on Nuclear Power Plants — meaning a `250%` overclocked Nuclear Plant (`600 m³/min`) stalls whenever trickles sit below `10 m³` inside its input buffer.
items.stepByStep:
1. When upgrading Fuel Generators from Fuel -> Turbofuel -> Rocket Fuel -> Ionized Fuel, flush only the pipelines (`Ctrl` hot-swap or Flush Net); leave the Fuel Generators connected so they auto-flush themselves.
2. Pre-fill every Nuclear Power Plant's `50 m³` water slot and feed `250%` Nuclear Plants (`600 m³/min`) via dedicated `600 m³/min` or `2x 300 m³/min` pre-filled lines.
items.proof: `AFGBuildableGeneratorFuel::Factory_CollectFuel` (`0x180531cb0`) calls `RemoveAllFromIndex` on `mFuelInventory` (`+0x838`) on fuel-class mismatch and pulls `GetSlotSize - CurrentAmount` (`50,000` L = `50 m³`) via `Factory_Internal_PullPipeInput` (`0x1808cb220`). `CanLoadSupplemental` (`0x18052d290`) & `LoadSupplemental` (`0x180541920`) check `mSupplementalLoadAmount` (`1000` L Coal vs `10000` L Nuclear).
